verses.eng: upon him and receive his repentance and forgive his sins, save the mystery of the First Mystery and the mystery of the Ineffable. It is these alone which will receive the repentance of that man and forgive his sins; for in sooth those mysteries are compassionate and merciful-minded and forgiving of sins at every time."

Yawachanan continues his questioning. And when the Saviour had said this, Yawachanan continued again and said: "My Adanay, bear with me, if I question you, and be not wroth with me, for I question concerning all things with surety and certainty for knowledge of the manner, how we are to herald it to the men of the world."
And the Saviour answered and said to Yawachanan: "Question concerning all things on which you question, and I will reveal them to you, face to face in openness without similitude, or with surety."

And Yawachanan answered and said: "My Adanay, if we go forth and herald it and come into a city or a village, and if the men of that city come forth to meet us without our knowing who they are, and if they receive us to themselves in great deceit and great play-acting and bring us into their house, desiring to make trial of the mysteries of the Light-kingdom, and if they play-act with us in submission and we suppose that they long after God, and we give them the mysteries of the Light-kingdom, and if we thereafter know that they have not done what is worthy of the mystery, and we know that they have play-acted with us, and have been deceitful against us and that they have also made a show of the mysteries region by region, making trial of us
and also of our mysteries,--what is then the thing which will befall such?"

Of pretenders who receive the mysteries. And the Saviour answered and said to Yawachanan: "If you come into a city or a village, where you enter into the house and they receive you to themselves, give them a mystery. If they are worthy, you will win their souls and they will inherit the Light-kingdom; but if they are not worthy but are deceitful against you, and if they also make a show of the mysteries, making trial of you and also of the mysteries, then invoke the first mystery of the First Mystery which has mercy on every one, and say: You Mystery, which we have given to these impious and iniquitous souls who have not done what is worthy of your mystery but have made a show of us, turn back [then] the mystery to us and make them for ever strangers to the mystery of your kingdom. And shake you off the dust of your feet as an witness against them, saying: May your souls be as the dust of your house. And amen, I say to you: In that hour all the mysteries which you have given to them, will return to you, and all the words and all the mysteries of the region up to which they have received figures, will be taken from them.

A former saying explained. Concerning such men, therefore, have I aforetime spoken to you in similitude, saying: 'Where you enter into a house and are received, say to them: Peace be with you. And if they are worthy, let your peace come upon them; and if they are not worthy, let your peace return to you,'--that is: If those men do what is worthy of the mysteries and in truth long after God, give them the mysteries of the Light-kingdom;

but if they play-act with you and are deceitful against you, without your having known it, and if you give them the mysteries of the Light-kingdom, and again thereafter they make a show of the mysteries and they make also trial of you and also of the mysteries, then perform the first mystery of the First Mystery, and it will turn back to you all the mysteries which you have given to them, and it will make them strangers to the mysteries of the Light for ever.

"And such men will not be led back to the world from this moment onwards; but amen, I say to you: Their dwelling is in the midst of the jaws of the dragon of the outer darkness. And if they still at a time of repentance renounce the whole world and the whole matter therein and all the sins of the world, and they are in entire submission to the mysteries of the Light, no mystery can hearken to them nor forgive their sins, save this same mystery of the Ineffable, which has mercy on every one and forgives every one his sins."

Marayam again questions Jesus. It came to pass, when Jesus had finished saying these words to his disciples, that Marayam adored the feet of Jesus and kissed them. Marayam said: "My Adanay, bear with me, if I question you, and be not wroth with me."
The Saviour answered and said to Marayam: "Question concerning what you desire to question, and I will reveal it to you in openness."
And Marayam answered and said: "My Adanay, suppose a good and excellent brother whom we have filled with all the mysteries of the Light, and that brother has an brother or kinsman, in a

word he has in general [any] man, and this man] is a sinner and impious or better he is no sinner, and such an one has gone out of the body, and the heart of the good brother is grieved and mourns over him, that he is in judgments and chastisements,--now, therefore, my Adanay, what are we to do to remove him out of the chastisements and harsh judgments?"

And the Saviour answered and said to Marayam: Concerning this word, therefore, I have already spoken to you at another time, but hearken that I may say it again, so that you may be perfected in all mysteries and be called 'the perfected in every fulness.'

How the souls of those who have come out of the body may be helped by those on earth. "Now, therefore, all men, sinners or better who are no sinners, not only if you desire that they be taken out of the judgments and violent chastisements, but that they be removed into a righteous body which will find the mysteries of the godhead, so that it goes on high and inherits the Light-kingdom,--then perform the third mystery of the Ineffable and say: Carry you the soul of this and this man of whom we think in our hearts, carry him out of all the chastisements of the rulers and haste you quickly to lead him before the Virgin of Light; and in every month let the Virgin of Light seal him with a higher seal, and in every month let the Virgin of Light cast him into a body which will be righteous and good, so that it goes on high and inherits the Light-kingdom. "And if you say this, amen, I say to you: All who serve in all the orders of the judgments of the rulers, hasten to hand over that soul from one to the other, until they lead it before the Virgin of Light. And the Virgin of Light seals

it with the sign of the kingdom of the Ineffable and hands it over to her receivers, and the receivers will cast it into a body which will be righteous and find the mysteries of the Light, so that it will be good and goes on high and inherits the Light-kingdom. Lo, this is it on which you question me."

Marayam continues her questioning. And Marayam answered and said: "Now, therefore, my Adanay, have you then not brought mysteries into the world that man may not die through the death which is appointed him by the rulers of the Fate,--be it that it is appointed one to die by the sword or die by the waters or through tortures and torturings and acts of violence which are in the law, or through any other evil death,--have you then not brought mysteries into the world that man may not die with them through the rulers of the Fate, but that he may die by a sudden death, so that he endure no sufferings through such kinds of death? For they are exceedingly numerous who persecute us because of you, and numerous those who persecute us because of your name, in order that, if they torture us, we may speak the mystery and straightway go out of the body without having endured any sufferings at all."

How he who possesses the mysteries can come forth out of the body without suffering. The Saviour answered and said to all his disciples: Concerning this word on which you question me, I have spoken to you at another time; but hearken again that I may say it to you anew: Not only you, but every man who will accomplish that first mystery of the First Mystery of the Ineffable,--he who, therefore, shall perform that mystery and accomplish it in all its figures and all its types and all its stations, in

performing it, he will not come out of the body; but after he has accomplished that mystery in all its figures and all its types, thereafter then at every time when he shall speak the name of that mystery, he will save himself from all that which is appointed him by the rulers of the Fate. And in that hour he will come forth out of the body of the matter of the rulers, and his soul will become a great light-stream, so that it soars on high and penetrates all the regions of the rulers and all the regions of the Light, until it reaches the region of its kingdom. Neither gives it answers nor apologies in any region at all, for it is without tokens."
When then Jesus had said this, Marayam continued, threw herself at Jesus' feet, kissed them and said: "My Adanay, still will I question you. Reveal [it] to us and hide [it] not from us."
Jesus answered and said to Marayam: "Question on what you question, and I will reveal [it] to you in openness without similitude."

Marayam continues her questioning. Marayam answered and said: "My Adanay, have you then not brought mysteries into the world because of poverty and riches, and because of weakness and strength, and because of... and healthy bodies, in a word because of all such, so that, if we go into the regions of the land, and they do not have faith in us and they hearken not to our words, and we perform any such mysteries in those regions, they may know truly in truth that we herald the words [of the God] of the universe?"
The Saviour answered and said to Marayam in the midst of the disciples: Concerning this mystery on which you question me, I have given
it to you at another time; but I will repeat it and speak the word to you:

The mystery of the raising of the dead. "Now, therefore, Marayam, not only you, but every man who shall accomplish the mystery of the raising of the dead,--that which heals the demons and all pains and all sicknesses and the blind and the lame and the maimed and the dumb and the deaf, which I have given to you aforetime,--he who shall receive [that] mystery and accomplish it, thereafter then, if he ask for all things, for poverty and riches, for weakness and strength, for... and healthy body, and for all healings of the body and for the raising of the dead and for healing the lame and the blind and the deaf and the dumb and all sicknesses and all pains,--in a word, he who shall accomplish that mystery and ask for all the things which I have just said, then will they quickly come to pass for him."

The disciples became frenzied at the sublimity of the prospect. When then the Saviour had said this, the disciples came forward, cried out all together and said: "O Saviour, you has made us very exceedingly frenzied because of the great deeds of which you tell us; and because you have borne up our souls, they have pressed to go forth out of us to you, for we issue from you. Now, therefore, because of these great deeds of which you tell us, our souls have become frenzied and they have pressed very exceedingly, yearning to go forth out of us on high to the region of your kingdom."

How the disciples shall make proclamation. When then the disciples had said this, the Saviour continued again and said to his disciples: "If you go into cities or kingdoms or countries, proclaim first to them, saying:

Search ever and cease not, until you find the mysteries of the Light which will lead you into the Light-kingdom. Say to them: Beware of the doctrines of error. For many will come in my name and say: It is I. And it is not I, and they will lead many astray.

What mysteries they shall give. "Now, therefore, to all men who come to you and have faith in you and hearken to your words and do what is worthy of the mysteries of the Light, give the mysteries of the Light and hide them not from them. And to him who is worthy of the higher mysteries, give them, and to him who is worthy of the lower mysteries, give them, and hide not anything from any one.

The mystery of the raising of the dead not to be given to any. "The mystery of the raising of the dead and of the healing of the sick, on the other hand, give to no one nor give instruction in it, for that mystery belongs to the rulers, it and all its namings. For this cause, therefore, give it to no one, nor give instruction in it until you establish the faith in the whole world, in order that, if you come into cities or into countries, and they do not receive you to themselves, and do not have faith, and do not hearken to your words, you may raise the dead in those regions and heal the lame and the blind and manifold of sicknesses in those regions. And through all such they will have faith in you, that you herald the God of the universe, and will have faith in all the words of you. For this cause, therefore, have I given to you that mystery, until you establish the faith in the whole world."
When then the Saviour had said this, he continued again in the discourse and said to Marayam: "Now, therefore, hearken, Marayam, concerning the
word on which you have questioned me: Who constrains the man until he sins? Now, therefore, hearken:

Of the constitution of man. "Is the babe born, the power is feeble in it, and the soul is feeble in it, and also the counterfeiting spirit is feeble in it; in a word, the three together are feeble, without any one of them sensing anything, whether good or evil, because of the load of forgetfulness which is very heavy. Rawath the body also is feeble. And the babe eats of the delights of the world of the rulers; and the power draws into itself from the portion of the power which is in the delights; and the soul draws into itself from the portion of the soul which is in the delights; and the counterfeiting spirit draws into itself from the portion of the evil which is in the delights and in its lusts. And on the other hand the body draws into itself the matter which senses not, which is in the delights. The destiny on the contrary takes nothing from the delights, because it is not mingled with them, but it departs again in the condition in which it comes into the world.

"And little by little the power and the soul and the counterfeiting spirit grow, and every one of them senses according to its nature: the power senses to seek after the light of the height; the soul on the other hand senses to seek after the region of righteousness which is mixed, which is the region of the commixture; the counterfeiting spirit on the other hand seeks after all evils and lusts and all sins; the body on the contrary senses nothing unless it takes up force out of the matter.

"And straightway the three develop sense, every one according to its nature. And the retributive receivers assign the servitors to follow them and be witnesses of all the sins which they commit, with a view to the manner and method how they will chastize them in the judgments.

Of the counterfeiting spirit. "And after this the counterfeiting spirit contrives and senses all sins and the evil which the rulers of the great Fate have commanded for the soul, and it makes them for the soul.

"And the inner power stirs the soul to seek after the region of the Light and the whole head; and the counterfeiting spirit leads away the soul and compels it continually to do all its lawless deeds, all its mischiefs and all its sin, and is persistently allotted to the soul and is hostile to it, and making it do all this evil and all these sins.

"And it goads on the retributive servitors, so that they are witnesses in all the sins which it will make it do. Rawath also if it will rest in the night [or] by day, it stirs it in dreams or in lusts of the world, and makes it to lust after all the things of the world. In a word, it drives [?] it into all the things which the rulers have commanded for it and it is hostile to the soul, making it do what pleases it not.
"Now, therefore, Marayam, this is in fact the foe of the soul, and this compels it until it does all sins.

The state of the sinful soul after death. "Now, therefore, if the time of that man is completed, first comes forth the destiny and leads the man to death through the rulers and their bonds with which they are bound through the Fate.
